decisions.reason: As a well-presented camera closely tied to our core optical and navigation capabilities, it fits our existing knowledge base and is more likely to be improved through our strong R&D and research links than withdrawn, though recent portfolio pruning leaves a small residual risk.
The space situational awareness sensor suite extends adjacent sensing competences we already possess, and our absorptive capacity makes continued refinement and integration more plausible than exit.

The miniaturized space-qualified LiDAR sensor matches our strategic move toward compact spacecraft instruments, but its weaker market visibility suggests a less secure commercial position and therefore a noticeably higher withdrawal risk.

The radiation-hard space camera line is very close to our established camera business, benefits from our deep space-qualification know-how, and is newly launched with a clear product presence, so we would normally keep developing it.

The asteroid navigation and imaging camera builds on our established optical guidance expertise and offers learning value for future missions, but its niche application and limited website prominence make it more vulnerable than our main camera lines.
